findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how record_criterion_verdict serializes concurrent same-turn writes to the run-scoped bank (e.g. a per-run write lock or atomic write-then-rename per criterion_id entry), matching the memo layer's per-signature lock precedent, so the idempotent upsert is truly atomic and not a TOCTOU race.
evidence: Plan: 'Fail-loud (any read/write error aborts recovery with a typed error), schema-versioned, idempotent upsert by criterion_id.'
Plan: 'run-unique git-ignored dir ... so concurrent closes cannot collide' addresses only CROSS-run collision.
agent_call.py:95: 'pydantic-ai runs a turn's tool calls concurrently'; the memo layer serializes this exact hazard with a per-signature asyncio.Lock (agent_call.py:108-129).
findings.finding: The run-scoped bank's 'idempotent upsert by criterion_id' defends against cross-run collision (run-unique dir) but not against two record_criterion_verdict calls issued in the SAME turn: pydantic-ai runs a turn's tool calls concurrently (agent_call.py:95, the reason the memo layer holds a per-signature asyncio.Lock), so concurrent read-modify-write against a shared schema-versioned bank store is a TOCTOU race that can tear or drop a banked verdict.
findings.location: Approach / Run-scoped bank; new completion_banking.py
scenarios: The verifier emits two record_criterion_verdict calls for different criteria in one turn; both read the bank file, both rewrite it, and one write clobbers the other's entry (lost banked verdict, silently reducing coverage).
A single per-criterion write is itself non-atomic (write-then-rename absent), leaving a torn schema-versioned file that the successor preflight then reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Write each criterion as its OWN file (bank/<criterion_id>.json) via atomic write-then-rename, or guard the single-file upsert with a per-run lock, and state this in the completion_banking.py scope so concurrent same-turn tool calls cannot tear or lose a banked entry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Analyze and state the lever-2 x runaway-guard interaction: whether path-normalized read caching changes the guard's range-sensitive distinct-ratio trip behavior, and confirm the guard still bounds varied-range re-read loops (or explicitly assign that bounding to the lever-1 budget floor instead of the guard).
evidence: Plan (lever 1): 'the surplus is spent on the measured 77%-re-read waste the runaway guard then correctly catches.'
Plan (lever 2): re-reads 'slip past' the exact-signature memo because ranges differ — the same reason they are DISTINCT signatures to the runaway guard.

agent_call.py:166-177: the guard appends tool_call_signature(name,tool_args) (range-sensitive) and trips only when window_distinct_ratio falls to REPETITION_TRIP_RATIO; the guard is wrapped OUTERMOST of the memo (agent_call.py:239-246), so it scores the raw call, not the cache hit.
findings.finding: The plan's lever-1 rationale relies on the runaway guard 'correctly catching' the 77% read_file re-read waste, but lever 2 collapses those re-reads while the runaway guard (agent_call.py:246, OUTERMOST) still keys its distinct-ratio window on the full signature INCLUDING line ranges — so varied-range re-reads remain DISTINCT to the guard and never dipped its ratio, and lever 2 alters the guard's observed call distribution without the plan analyzing whether that suppresses or delays a legitimate runaway trip.
findings.location: Approach / lever 1 + lever 2; agent_call.py:145-180, 239-246
scenarios: A verifier loops re-reading one file at many distinct ranges: lever 2 makes each cheap, the guard's distinct-ratio stays high (each range is distinct), so the guard never trips and the run instead runs to its (now smaller, lever-1) budget floor — the plan's claimed 'guard catches the waste' safety net does not fire on precisely the waste pattern lever 2 targets.
Collapsing repeated-signature reads (exact repeats) changes the distinct-ratio the guard computes, potentially delaying or altering when it trips on genuinely pathological loops.
